# Google Threat Intelligence Threat Lists Feed – XSOAR Integration

Here's what I found about the **Google Threat Intelligence Threat Lists** feed integration for Cortex XSOAR and its `gti-threatlists-get-indicators` command.

## Overview

Use this feed integration to fetch Google Threat Intelligence Threat Lists matches as indicators. It processes the latest finished job retrieving its matches based on the limit parameter (10 by default) in every fetch until there are no more matches for that job.

## The `gti-threatlists-get-indicators` Command

This command gets the matches from Google Threat Intelligence Threat Lists. Note that there is no context output for this command. It can be run from the Cortex XSOAR CLI, as part of an automation, or in a playbook. After you successfully execute a command, a DBot message appears in the War Room with the command details.

**Example usage:**
!gti-threatlists-get-indicators !gti-threatlists-get-indicators feed=malware package=2025021910 filter="gti_score:70+" limit=10

## Configuration Steps

To set up the instance in XSOAR:
- Navigate to Settings > Integrations > Servers & Services. Search for Google Threat Intelligence Threat Lists. Click Add instance to create and configure a new integration instance.
- Set a name for the instance, select the option "Fetches indicators," and introduce your API KEY.
- Set a Filter (if needed) for your Threat List (e.g., "gti_score:70+ positives:10- has:campaigns"). Configure the maximum number of results to return; if 0, all results will be returned. Set a Feed Fetch Interval. Adjust the Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) designation to apply to indicators fetched from the feed.
- Click Test to validate the URLs, token, and connection.

## Available Threat Lists

There are 14 categorized threat lists: cryptominer, first-stage-delivery-vectors, infostealer, iot, linux, malicious-network-infrastructure, malware, mobile, osx, phishing, ransomware, threat-actor, trending and vulnerability-weaponization. The access to these threat lists depends on your Google TI license type.

Regarding license tiers: Customers can access a subset of the available threat lists based on their GTI tier — GTI Standard: Ransomware, Malicious Network Infrastructure; GTI Enterprise: Ransomware, Malicious Network Infrastructure, Malware, Threat Actor, Daily Top Trending; GTI Enterprise+: Access to all available threat lists.

## Requirements & Compatibility

- Threat Lists component compatibility: XSOAR 5.5.0 and later.
- You need administrator access to your XSOAR instance to install the application.
- A valid Google TI API key is required to authenticate. It is strongly recommended to use a service account API key rather than a key tied to an individual user account, as service account keys are better suited for automated systems.
- Note that the usage of this integration entails API quota consumption.

## Common Use Case

This component is particularly useful for automated threat prevention. Teams can ingest the indicators available from Google TI's categorized Threat Lists (feeds). These indicators are related to specific threat types, and are used to feed them directly into defensive systems, such as firewalls and web proxies to block threats before an alert is even generated.

## Technical Background on the Underlying API

The feed relies on the GTI Threat Lists API, where Threat Lists are hourly generated as IoCs packages, with 2 hours difference from the current time. This means that if the current time in UTC is T, you can get the T-2h Threat List but any more recent than that. This endpoint returns the last generated IoCs package.

For the most complete and up-to-date reference, you can visit the official [Cortex XSOAR documentation page](https://xsoar.pan.dev/docs/reference/integrations/google-threat-intelligence-threat-lists) and the [Google TI XSOAR integration guide](https://gtidocs.virustotal.com/docs/gti4xsoar-guide).
